title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Daily Brief (27 October 2026)
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart or readership statistics. This is a relevance-ranked selection from an incomplete biomedical preprint corpus; bioRxiv, medRxiv, and the broader medical literature are not covered. Semantic Scholar citation totals are current totals, not gains during this window, and sparse signals do not support a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: The 27 October 2026 announcement batch contributes seven notable papers in this focused selection, led by computational protein/RNA methods, CRISPR-screen interpretation, and miRNA benchmarking. The list is ranked by relevance and evidence type, not measured popularity.

sections.title: Agent-guided epitope excision enables economical de novo binder design
sections.abstract: The authors crop protein targets to local binding-site windows and combine this with an agent-guided design loop, reporting faster structure-design computation and yeast-display-enriched binders, including four tested clones with nanomolar apparent affinity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports a median interface Cα RMSD of 0.37 Å for cropped versus full targets and about 88% lower RFdiffusion/AlphaFold3 GPU time for one FAP epitope. At a fixed budget, the human-in-the-loop arm's computational hit rate was 9.33% versus 5.06% for the PI-alone arm; yeast display recovered enriched designs, and four representative clones showed apparent KD values of 3.0–9.1 nM.
sections.unique_caveat: Wet-lab evidence is yeast display, not in-vivo efficacy or therapeutic validation. The autonomy comparison used one large target (FAP), one backbone class, and one LLM controller; authors identify soluble-binder characterization, FAP specificity, and inhibition assays as future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 15-target/3,666-design benchmark plus wet-lab yeast display; Semantic Scholar snapshot: zero citations and zero influential citations.

sections.title: Escaping cells dilute CRISPR screen responses unequally across cell types
sections.abstract: Reanalysis of published single-cell CRISPR screens estimates the fraction of measured cells that escaped effective knockdown and argues that this cell-type-dependent fraction can dilute perturbation responses and distort cross-cell comparisons and benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author defines an escape fraction estimated from each cell's target-gene counts. In reported analyses, it rose with gene essentiality and reached roughly one half in human embryonic stem cells for some essential perturbations; the estimate tracked response dilution and affected a simple cross-cell transfer model and benchmark scoring.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a reanalysis, not a new controlled CRISPR experiment. The inferred escape fraction is checked against simulations and measured dilution, not independent per-cell protein-level measurement; datasets differ by study and protocol.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Published-screen reanalysis spanning 13 cell types/states, with seven datasets supporting per-perturbation estimates and simulation/replicate checks; Semantic Scholar snapshot: zero citations and zero influential citations.

sections.title: Benchmarking miRNA Target Prediction Methods
sections.abstract: Seven miRNA–mRNA prediction tools are compared over about 59.7 million candidate pairs using an evidence-graded reference combining two validated-interaction databases with paired RNA-seq evidence from an iPSC cohort.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that TargetScan and miRDB maintained Type I error below 0.05 across their settings but had limited power; mirDIP had the highest power but more false positives. No tool led on every metric, so tool and cutoff selection should reflect the sensitivity/specificity trade-off.
sections.unique_caveat: The expression component comes from one iPSC cohort—five 22q11.2 deletion syndrome donor lines and five controls—and the reference combines incomplete databases with expression-derived evidence rather than a gold-standard assay for all pairs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in genomics and quantitative biology; seven tools and 59,734,204 candidate pairs; arXiv comment reports acceptance at IEEE BIBM 2026. Semantic Scholar snapshot: zero citations and zero influential citations.

sections.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
sections.abstract: The paper releases a curated all-atom molecular-dynamics dataset for 48 RNA systems, with coordinates, forces, structural annotations, and replica-exchange metadata for data-driven RNA models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report REST2 simulations with 32 Hamiltonian states and 200–300 ns production per state, plus force labels evaluated at sampled and unscaled reference Hamiltonians; they characterize sampling, exchange, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions.
sections.unique_caveat: These are simulation ensembles, not experimental observations of RNA conformational populations. Coverage is 48 selected systems and the force-field/sampling choices bound downstream use.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across q-bio.BM, cs.LG, and physics.bio-ph; reusable molecular-method dataset. Semantic Scholar snapshot: zero citations and zero influential citations.

sections.title: MechGate: combining mechanism-derived measures of permeation and efflux to screen small molecule drugs targeting Escherichia coli
sections.abstract: MechGate combines computational measures of porin and membrane permeation, efflux, and antibacterial activity to identify which modeled barrier may impede candidate small molecules against E. coli.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint presents five readouts from SMILES input and reports external marketed-antibacterial-set precision of 0.789–0.873 for component measures and 0.92 for a combined rule, compared with baselines near 0.44.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational screening, not an antibacterial efficacy experiment. The authors report source-library separability by physicochemical properties and build comparisons within each library; prospective experimental validation is needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Mechanism-focused antibiotic screening, external set of marketed antibacterials and reported component/combined precision; Semantic Scholar snapshot: zero citations and zero influential citations.

sections.title: Regional prediction of hematoma expansion from non-contrast computed tomography in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage patients
sections.abstract: A regional transport-based morphometry model is derived on one intracerebral-hemorrhage cohort and tested on a separate archive to predict hematoma expansion from admission CT scans.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a combined regional model validation AUROC of 0.787 in VISTA-ICH and identify size, heterogeneity, eccentricity, and peripheral density patterns as regional features.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective model validation is not evidence of improved clinical decisions or patient outcomes. The authors describe evidence as preliminary; prospective validation, calibration, and cross-site evaluation remain needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Explicit derivation/validation split: 574 ERICH patients and 196 VISTA-ICH patients; no Semantic Scholar Graph match returned at snapshot time.

sections.title: Tau creates spatially moving hotspots of amyloid-β secondary nucleation: a reaction-diffusion model
sections.abstract: A reaction-diffusion model predicts that tau-driven amyloid-β nucleation can create a moving spatial maximum in secondary-nucleation activity as fibril growth depletes free monomer near the source.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author derives a condition for an interior nucleation-rate maximum and simulates possible separation between tau burden, fibril-mass growth, and instantaneous amyloid-β secondary-nucleation activity.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical model, not an experiment or clinical finding. The spatial pattern depends on assumptions about oligomer transport, exchange, and site density and needs spatially resolved biochemical testing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Molecular mechanism question with explicit transport/turnover parameters and testable spatial predictions; no Semantic Scholar Graph match returned at snapshot time.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Across the selected set, recurring themes are benchmark and measurement reliability; scaling computational molecular workflows while preserving evidence boundaries; and a spectrum of translational evidence from modeling to retrospective validation.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: Follow-up work includes testing binder generalization across targets and scaffolds, directly measuring knockdown and cell survival in matched CRISPR screens, validating miRNA predictions in independent cohorts and assays, prospectively testing antibiotic permeability and efflux predictions, comparing RNA simulations with experimental ensembles, prospectively validating the CT model, and testing the tau model's spatial predictions with controlled gradients.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The strongest contributions pair computational methods with explicit validation boundaries: one binder study has early in-vitro follow-up, CRISPR and miRNA papers expose benchmark assumptions, and the imaging model has retrospective external validation. No paper can be called popular from available attention signals.
